text:
Utah's 4-1 win over Buffalo was the result its play had been building toward since the opening period. UTA out-chanced BUF 1.79 to 0.43 in expected goals in the first, and the final tally was 4.42 to 2.79 across the night. By the simulation, UTA deserved to win 74 percent of the time. The one thing Buffalo did early was cash a 6 percent power-play chance: Tage Thompson's wrist shot at 8:00, set up by Rasmus Dahlin, made it 1-0. Kailer Yamamoto answered at 10:12 with a 60 percent look to tie it, and Utah never trailed again.

The second period was where the game turned. Nick Schmaltz scored on the power play at 15:23, a wrist shot off passes from Logan Cooley and Clayton Keller, and Anders Lee added a backhand at 17:24 to make it 3-1. John Marino then scored on a 4 percent slap shot on the power play at 1:45 of the third, the least likely goal of the night. Utah went 2 for 5 on the power play against Buffalo's 1 for 4, and the Sabres took 15 penalty minutes to Utah's 23.

Karel Vejmelka was the quiet difference. He faced 24 shots, allowed one, and saved 1.79 goals more than expected, including a 31 percent third-period chance from Noah Ostlund. Buffalo did push back late, with an expected goals edge of 1.72 to 1.25 in the third, but Vejmelka stopped what mattered. Colten Ellis was close to par, 0.42 goals above expected. Marino, Lee and Yamamoto took the three stars, each with a goal and an assist.
